status: 50 complete own Urdu fields read before viewing any phase14 proposed candidate
selection_scope: First 50 numerically ordered unread Urdu occurrences within the original Abu Dawud/Tirmidhi 636 manual ledger; not the different global manual-plus-reuse selection.
scope: Independent complete supplied-field reading for attribution and quotation boundaries only. No authenticity, transcription, canonical-edition identity or unread-language certification. Initial notes remain historical if later exact-boundary refinements are accepted.

fields.initial_source_first_note: Complete Urdu field read. Salman’s actual question-and-answer supplies the specific qibla/right-hand/fewer-than-three-stones/dung-and-bone prohibitions. The parenthetic mockery/pride descriptions are interpretive tone glosses and can remain context; preserve the actual question, yes-answer and all four objects/conditions.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the Prophet’s orientation instruction separately from Abu Ayyub’s subsequent Syria observation, turning-away practice and forgiveness request. Retain the parenthetic Abu Ayyub says attribution at the voice transition. The numeric footnote is context; no geographic/legal reconciliation is added.

Complete Urdu field read. The actual prohibition concerns both qiblas and is expressly attributed. The parenthetic place names identify the already stated pair and can remain contextual glosses. The final Abu Dawud note identifying Abu Zayd as Banu Thalaba’s servant is chain/identity apparatus, not another narrated prohibition.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the initial prohibition and Jabir’s later one-year-before-death observation. The contrasting link and bodily-need circumstance matter: deleting the latter would turn the observed act into generic qibla-facing and erase the stated contrast. Only the numeric marker is apparatus; no harmonization is attempted.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the greeting, delayed reply, wudu, actual parenthetic return-greeting action, apology and purity statement. The final narrator uncertainty between two Arabic purity phrases is transmission wording apparatus; keep it as context rather than inventing a preferred reading. Preserve the source pronoun shift.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the two graves, punishment statement, urine/gossip descriptions, split branch actions and the complete until-dry alleviation statement. The buried-in-grave identification is explanatory context. Hannad’s final Arabic-word comparison and its rendering are compiler variant apparatus; no missing report is reconstructed from them.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the standing-urination/water/wudu/khuff account and the separately supplied finite Hudhayfa approach/heel-position addition quoted through Musaddad by Abu Dawud. The dungheap synonym and footnote are context. Parenthetic wudu, coming and posture words supply actual scene actions; do not blanket-remove the quoted addition merely because it follows a compiler introduction.

Complete Urdu field read. Umayma bint Ruqayqa supplies the recurring bowl-under-bed/night-use report. Preserve the doubled کہ and the parenthetic habitual-kept predicate as source narrative, with no name or grammar correction.

Complete Urdu field read. Humayd describes meeting an unnamed companion whose association is compared with Abu Hurayra’s. Do not rename that person Abu Hurayra. Keep the actual daily-combing and bath-place-urination prohibitions under the unnamed companion’s transmitted Prophetic report.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Aisha’s full right-hand wudu/eating and left-hand bodily-need/filth account. The paired purposes are actual source content, without a compiler tail or missing-body pointer.

Complete Urdu field read. The jug synonym is lexical context. Preserve the greeting-free water dialogue, the complete not-commanded-every-time negation and the final conditional. The wajibah parenthesis qualifies the claimed obligation status of the resulting practice and should stay; removing it would change the normative claim.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the counterfactual hardship condition and both stated proposed commands: delayed Isha and miswak at every prayer. Do not drop one clause or replace the source with a more familiar parallel.
Complete Urdu field read. Shurayh’s actual question and Aisha’s miswak answer describe the Prophet’s entry practice. Preserve the named dialogue and concise complete answer.

Complete long Urdu field read. Keep the night waking, miswak, actual Quranic quotation, near-complete-or-complete surah uncertainty, repeated two-unit cycles and Witr. The numeric marker and parenthetic restatement of the already described same-action sequence are explanatory context. Abu Dawud’s final Ibn Fudayl/Husayn variant supplies a finite miswak/wudu/recitation-to-surah-end report; retain that actual variant separately and qualify its transmitted attribution, without erasing it as mere compiler introduction.
Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Aisha’s shared-vessel bathing report and the explicit state of both participants. All words form the finite source account; no outside interpretation is added.

Complete Urdu field read. The four-year companion remains unnamed despite the Abu Hurayra comparison. Keep the bidirectional leftover-water prohibition. Musaddad’s addition supplies an actual simultaneous-handful instruction, but its ultimate speaker is not explicitly restated here; qualify that finite transmitted addition instead of inventing direct Prophetic wording or calling it Musaddad’s personal ruling.

Complete Urdu field read. The same complete Aisha/Prophet brass-vessel bathing report is printed twice. Preserve both source copies or their fully explicit source context, without silently deduplicating the bytes or counting them as two provider occurrences; one source report family can represent the repeated wording.
Complete Urdu field read. Abdullah ibn Zayd reports the visit, drawing water in a brass bowl and the Prophet’s ablution. The complete short event has no side-note apparatus or unseen text to fill.

Complete Urdu field read. The introductory full-hadith pointer is not itself a supplied body, but the field then supplies Ali’s head wiping, near-dripping water, threefold foot washing and explicit this-was-the-Prophet’s-wudu statement. Retain that finite demonstration under the local Zirr/Ali framing, without reconstructing the omitted earlier actions.

Complete Urdu field read. Abu Hayya describes Ali’s actual washing, head wiping, feet-to-ankles and stated wish to demonstrate the Prophet’s wudu. The ibn-Qays identity, limbs clarification and final how-he-performed-wudu restatement are explanatory glosses; preserve the actual demonstration and spoken wish without inventing a fuller account.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Miqdam’s full ablution observation, every threefold count, the source’s own wrists wording, and wiping the head and both outside and inside of the ears. Do not silently replace a source limb term with a parallel version.

Complete Urdu field read. Ibn Abbas asks whether to show the Prophet’s wudu and then performs a one-wash-per-limb demonstration. Keep the question and demonstration as his reported example, not a newly invented direct Prophetic command.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the source’s Talha-grandfather/Kab ibn Amr Yami identification as supplied, the visit, water running from face and beard to chest, and the separate mouth/nose actions. The footnote marker is apparatus; do not correct the printed identity against another source.

Complete Urdu field read. The opening Laqit visit to Aisha is itself a finite historical clause, followed by an omitted-story pointer and a supplied finite arrival of the Prophet leaning forward. Keep those actual clauses with their own attribution. The same-meaning pointer, explanation of leaning as fast walking, and final khazira/asida food-word comparison are context; do not invent the omitted meal or story.

Complete Urdu field read. The initial Ibn Jurayj same-report transmission pointer is context. The explicitly supplied Prophetic instruction to rinse the mouth when performing wudu is a finite body; preserve the condition and exact command.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep Mughira’s Tabuk ablution service and the actual top-and-bottom khuff wiping assertion. Abu Dawud’s appended Thawr/Raja hearing criticism is context and must remain visible. Do not correct the body or assign an independent authenticity grade.

Complete Urdu field read. The uncle’s full-name parenthesis is identity apparatus. Retain the parenthetic doubt that wudu had broken because it identifies the actual domain of the reported uncertainty; generic prayer doubt would broaden the claim. Preserve the complete until-sound-or-smell condition and prohibition on breaking prayer.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Talq’s visit, the unnamed questioner who only appeared rural, the after-wudu touching question, and the lump-or-piece wording uncertainty. The numeric marker is context; neither the questioner’s identity nor a preferred wording is supplied externally.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the shoulder eating, wiping the hand on the mat, standing and praying. This field does not expressly say that no wudu occurred; do not add that clause from its chapter or another edition. Preserve the printed wiping spelling.

Complete long Urdu field read. Keep Jabir’s battle/guard narrative, the unnamed pursuer’s vow, the Prophet’s guard request, the three-arrow episode and the actual Companions’ conversation. The pursuit restatement, companion-category gloss, Quran-in-prayer identification and footnote can be context; actual arrival and viewing-distance narrative circumstances should not be discarded merely for parentheses. No names for the two guards or a name for the recited surah are invented.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Anas’s companions-waiting/dozing/praying account with the sleep circumstance and no-repeat-wudu qualification. Abu Dawud’s quoted Shuba/Qatada addition supplies a finite first-person waiting/dozing report from the Prophet’s time and should retain qualified transmitted attribution. The final Ibn Abi Aruba different-wording pointer has no supplied body and is context.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the iqamah, unnamed man’s private request, all-or-some people sleeping uncertainty, and the Prophet leading prayer afterward. Thabit’s final omission-of-wudu notice is compiler/transmission context, not an affirmative claim that no wudu occurred.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Abu Hurayra’s retreat, bathing, return and actual dialogue ending in the Muslim-not-najis statement. The there-from departure gloss and went-away insertion in an otherwise complete where-were-you question are explanatory, while the actual departure and return verbs outside them stay. Do not change the source’s bodily-purity terms.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the source’s fifty prayers, sevenfold bathing/urine-washing requirements and later reductions without historical harmonization. The obligation predicate and the Prophet’s request-for-reduction object are meaningful supplied content; a generic asked clause would lose the claimed action. The time-slot identification alone can be contextual gloss.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the tightly braided hair question and both finite three-handful instructions, including the later whole-body/purity completion. The source distinguishes an unnamed Muslim woman from Zuhayr’s Umm Salama wording; retain that uncertainty visibly without silently identifying the first speaker. Compiler variant framing is not itself a separate Prophetic saying.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the actual woman’s arrival and Umm Salama’s reported question as well as the expressly supplied squeeze-your-locks-at-each-handful answer. The omitted same-report pointer is context. Do not reconstruct the missing question or bathing procedure.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the supplied Shurayh/Jubayr/Thawban reporting chain and the complete male/female bathing instructions: male hair opening and root wetting, no fault for a woman leaving hair braided, and three handfuls on the head. Do not replace these sex-specific source conditions with a generalized rule.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep Aisha’s repeated night/shared-cloth account and the two blood-contact/washing/praying sequences exactly. The body-contact parenthesis distinguishes the first target from the subsequent clothing clause and is a meaningful local circumstance. Preserve the source’s awkward repeated same-cloth phrasing without repair.

Complete Urdu field read. The initial same-event pointer is context, but the supplied leave-prayer/bathe/bind-cloth/pray instruction is finite. Retain the after-menstrual-blood-stops temporal qualification because the abridged outside-it wording alone omits its domain. Abu Dawud’s final Hammad/Ayyub identification of Fatima is compiler identity context, not a replacement for the local Umm Salama narrator.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the actual instruction’s onset/end conditions, blood washing and prayer. The parenthetic days identifies the already stated duration and can be contextual; the parenthetic bathing action is an actual prerequisite supplied in the field and should remain. Initial transmission/same-meaning pointer is context.

Complete Urdu field read. Bahiya reports hearing a woman ask Aisha, then Aisha’s first-person account of the Prophet instructing her to tell the woman supplies the body. Retain the parenthetic Aisha-says voice transition and the two stated alternatives for counting days. The problem noun is lexical context; the cycle/bathing/binding/prayer instructions remain exact.

Complete long Urdu field read. Distinguish the initial Fatima/Prophetic blood-color instruction from the later explicitly attributed Ibn Abbas, Makhul, Said ibn Musayyib, Hasan, Qatada, Taymi and Ibn Sirin statements. The compilation includes actual finite transmitted rulings and the final question/answer as well as unsupplied same-meaning and chain-comparison apparatus; never flatten those named voices into Prophetic speech. The latter apparatus can remain context, and any retained finite sayings require their own actual source attribution and no independent authenticity claim. The black-blood cessation qualification and the meaning of sitting out prayer affect the stated conditions, while the woman and vein-blood identification glosses may be contextual.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Aisha’s seven-year bleeding report, the Prophet’s bathing instruction, and Umm Habiba’s subsequent every-prayer bathing practice without turning that practice into an explicit every-prayer command. The conflicting Hamna name parenthesis is source identity context; do not resolve it with an external identity correction.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve Ikrima’s actual report and the wait-until-menstrual-days-end qualification: deleting the parenthetic ending would change the timing of the command. Keep the later conditional perception/wudu/prayer clause; only the numeric note marker is apparatus.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep Aisha’s lost-necklace mission, prayer without wudu and the reported revelation event. Ibn Nufayl’s addition supplies Usayd’s actual finite words to Aisha; retain them as separately attributed Companion speech, not a Prophetic quotation or mere compiler comment.

Complete long Urdu field read. Preserve Abu Wail’s witnessed Ibn Masud/Abu Musa disagreement, both actual views and reasons, the quoted Quran words with their supplied Urdu translation, Ammar’s reported mission/purity episode and the final objection involving Umar. The local Ammar-to-Umar speech relation is supplied attribution; a surah label must be distinguished from the actual recitation and question rather than deleting the verse itself.

Complete long Urdu field read. Preserve the unnamed questioner’s parenthetic no-water/junub conditions and actual question, Umar’s reply, Ammar’s recollection, the Prophet’s demonstration and their final exchange. The camel-herding expansion, earth synonym, footnote and final that-is restatement of the already complete Umar reply are explanatory context. Retain the source’s half-forearm wording without harmonizing it with a parallel.

Complete Urdu field read. Keep the expressly supplied Ammar-addressed response and demonstration, one ground strike, hand-on-hand movement, face/half-forearm wiping and explicit not-to-elbows limit. Abu Dawud’s final Waki/Jarir chain comparisons have no further supplied body and remain context.

Complete Urdu field read. The initial same-story transmission pointer is context. Retain the actual enough-to-do-this answer and the ground strike/blowing/face-and-palms action. Salama’s final elbows-versus-palms wording doubt and rendering are transmission apparatus retained visibly, without choosing a preferred body or completing the uncertain account.

Complete Urdu field read. Preserve the actual strike/face/palms instruction, with the full-hadith pointer as context. Abu Dawud then quotes two finite variant additions: Ammar’s sermon wording without blowing, and a transmitted strike-and-blow wording. Keep both with their actual chain/variant qualifications and the negation intact; do not discard actual quoted actions as all compiler prose or reconcile the conflicting variants.
